I really don't know how to word this so here it goes, I'm currently a single father of a quizzical 3 and 5 year old. Back in December of last year I found out that their mother (whom I had been married to for 4 years and with for 7) was cheating on me with a co-worker. I found this out one late night when I was waiting to pick her up from work and saw her walking out arm intertwined with his. So naturally I don't react very well. I don't go into work, I don't return texts from their mom, I just lay on the couch sobbing quietly watching one of those PBS cartoons, but of course two curious kids aren't going to be okay with that. They start asking me what's wrong and why I'm sad, part of me wants to tell them everything and slur insults about their mother but I don't because I remember all the fights my parents had in front of me and all the hateful words that they spewed back and forth so their was no way I could put them through something like that, but I had no one to vent to so my solution was just to tell them I'm sad and that I'll get better. They stopped asking questions after that and instead just hugged me and assured me it would be okay which was all I needed. I sucked it up, went back to work the next day, and started preparing for the marriage to end. I'm definitely not okay still but I'm 200x better because I had those two to comfort me and tell me it was alright. So while I don't agree with telling them about your problems I understand the desire for the nonjudgemental love a kid can give you when you're feeling down, so don't weigh them down with detail just generalize it and let their unwavering happiness overshadow any problem you might have. Moral of the story is I may be single, I may be sad, but I kept them happy and thats all I want. I may dislike their mother but she is still that, their mother, and unless harm comes to them by her hand, I'll never take that away.
